findings.title: FAILS THE SECOND CLAUSE DECISIVELY, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL READING IN THE SWEEP. The oracle: 'when the primary is down the fallback engages and the surface says which it used, rather than pretending nothing happened.' Two clauses, and this page is measured against both. MEASURED SIDE BY
findings.detail: FAILS THE SECOND CLAUSE DECISIVELY, AND THIS IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL READING IN THE SWEEP. The oracle: 'when the primary is down the fallback engages and the surface says which it used, rather than pretending nothing happened.' Two clauses, and this page is measured against both. MEASURED SIDE BY SIDE AT THE SAME URL (`/logbook.html`), online then offline with the cache warm: online the page renders 4,888 characters, **20 entries**, and pills reading `total-count=516`, `machine-count=30`, `open-count=6`. Offline it serves the REAL page (not the offline shell) with 777 characters, **0 entries**, pills reading `total-count=0`, `machine-count=0`, `open-count=0`, and `#empty-state` VISIBLE: **'No entries yet. Log your first repair to get started.'** **516 becomes 0 and the page calls it 'no entries yet'.** That is the definition of pretending nothing happened. A technician in a plant dead-zone - the exact user this PWA precaches 26 files for - opens their logbook and is told they have never logged a repair. AND THE BLAST RADIUS IS WHY IT MATTERS MOST HERE: `v_logbook_truth` feeds asset-hub, analytics, pm-scheduler, project-manager, resume, assistant, dayplanner, hive and index. This is the page whose record is a person's skill evidence. CORROBORATED BY THE 500 INJECTION, which is a different failure mode reaching the same screen: with 3 reads answered 500 the page shows 'No entries yet.' and no failure sentence at all. Two independent injections, one defect. TO FINISH: gate `#empty-state` and the three count pills on the read's outcome, so 'not loaded' is a third state beside 'loaded and empty' and 'failed'. hive is the in-repo reference for the wording - 'Could not reach your hive. Check your connection and refresh the page' - and inventory's own 'Stock levels are unknown right now, not zero' is the pattern for the pills. THERE IS NO READ FALLBACK ON THIS PLATFORM, AND THAT IS PROVEN FROM THE SERVICE WORKER'S SOURCE RATHER THAN INFERRED. `sw.js` handles API traffic in one branch - `if (url.includes('supabase.co') || url.includes('fonts.goog') ...) e.respondWith(fetch(e.request).catch(() => new Response('', { status: 503 })))` (sw.js:195-200) - so a failed read resolves to an EMPTY 503 body. And `cache.put` appears **nowhere in the file**, so no API response is ever stored: `caches.match()` cannot hit for a `/rest/v1/` URL because nothing put one there. The 26-entry `SHELL_FILES` precache holds HTML, CSS and JS only. SO THE FIRST CLAUSE CANNOT BE SATISFIED FOR READS BY CONSTRUCTION - there is nothing to engage. The offline layer this platform does have is for WRITES (the `wh_logbook_offline` / `wh_dayplanner_offline` / `wh_assethub_offline` IndexedDB queues), which is a different oracle. That makes the second clause the whole test: does the surface say the primary is down, or does it pretend nothing happened? MEASURED TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS, so the reading does not rest on one injection style. (1) Every `/rest/v1/` and `/rpc/` request answered with a synthetic 500 at `window.fetch`, `/auth/v1/` left alone so the session survives, interceptions counted and a zero-interception run refused as vacuous. (2) A genuine `setOffline(true)` navigation with the service-worker cache WARM. THE SECOND METHOD TOOK THREE ATTEMPTS TO GET HONEST, WHICH IS WHY IT IS TRUSTWORTHY NOW. Navigating to `/workhive/logbook.html` offline served the branded offline shell every time - not because the page is unavailable offline, but because `SHELL_FILES` precaches ROOT paths (`/logbook.html`) and the `/workhive/` prefix is a different cache key. Measured at the path the cache actually holds, the real page is served. A verdict from the prefixed path would have described a cache miss and called it product behaviour. AND ONE LIMIT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: under Playwright's `setOffline(true)`, `navigator.onLine` still read **true** and `wh-conn-chip` still read 'Online' (hidden). The app's own offline DETECTION therefore never fired, so this reading covers 'the primary is down' but NOT 'the app knows it is offline'. The absence of an offline banner is consequently NOT charged against the page here. A probe that wants that claim must also override `navigator.onLine` and dispatch the `offline` event.

TWO OPPOSITE CLA
findings.detail: FAILS at the in-flight state, and the contradiction is the finding. With 6 reads held in flight logbook renders **5 skeleton elements** - so it knows it is loading - AND SIMULTANEOUSLY a false-empty sentence matching 'no entries yet', plus **3 bare zeros** among 6 numbers on screen. TWO OPPOSITE CLAIMS IN ONE VIEW: the skeleton says 'still loading', the empty-state sentence says 'there is nothing here'. A reader resolves that with whichever they notice first, and the sentence is prose while the skeleton is decoration - so the wrong one usually wins. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE fail_500 DEFECT ALREADY FIXED ON THIS PAGE, one state earlier: there the counters read 0 after a FAILED read; here they read 0 (and 'no entries yet') while the read is merely SLOW. The error path was fixed by `_lbReadFailed` dashing the pills; the loading path needs the same treatment - while a read is in flight the empty-state must not render at all, and the pills should hold their skeleton rather than a zero. logbook is the platform's evidence base (v_logbook_truth feeds 11 consumers), so 'you have no entries' shown to someone with 516 of them is the most consequential version of this bug. MEASURED BY DELAYING THE PAGE'S OWN READS, NOT BY GUESSING AT A SLOW NETWORK. Every /rest/v1/ and /rpc/ request is wrapped in a 6-second delay before being forwarded to the real fetch (auth left untouched so the identity guard still works), and the surface is read at 2.2s - i.e. WHILE the reads are provably still in flight. Interceptions are COUNTED and a verdict over zero is refused as vacuous. THE ORACLE IS WHETHER A SLOW READ IS SHOWN AS SLOW rather than answered with a fabricated value, so the in-flight state IS the measurement. Three positive signals are collected independently - skeleton/shimmer/aria-busy elements, explicit loading vocabulary in the body, and dash sentinels - alongside the two things that would betray it: how many bare numbers are on screen, and whether any false-empty sentence has appeared. AN HONEST INSTRUMENT LIMIT, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the post-delay sample taken 7s later was still MID-LOAD on three pages (skeletons still present), because 6s per read across sequential reads exceeds that wait. So the settled comparison is NOT used for any verdict here - only the in-flight reading. Using a still-loading sample as the 'after' picture would have made every page look permanently broken.

findings.title: LEFT OWED BECAUSE THE ORACLE AS WORDED DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS WRITE, and forcing it either way would be the false reading.
findings.detail: LEFT OWED BECAUSE THE ORACLE AS WORDED DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS WRITE, and forcing it either way would be the false reading. The oracle asks that offline 'the write is refused BEFORE firing and the person is told NOTHING WAS SENT'. A logbook entry is field capture, and field capture on this platform is designed to QUEUE - so the honest offline behaviour here is the opposite of a refusal, and banking this green would credit a refusal that must not exist while banking it red would call a working feature a defect. WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY DOES, read directly rather than inferred: the entry save has an offline branch - `if (!navigator.onLine) { await queueEntryOffline(payload); _allEntries.unshift({...payload, _offline: true}); await updateOfflineBadge(); sync-badge.classList.remove('hidden'); showToast('Saved offline, will sync when connected.'); }`. So it holds the entry in the wh_logbook_offline IndexedDB store, shows it immediately marked _offline, reveals a sync badge, and says it will sync. That is queue-and-tell, and it is right: a technician writing up a breakdown in a plant basement must not lose the entry because the signal died. THE EDIT PATH QUEUES TOO, and its mechanism is worth recording because it carries this page's own invariant: an offline edit of an entry that was itself created offline re-queues via put() on the id keyPath, which REPLACES the pending insert rather than adding a second one - that is the offline-create-then-edit-collapses-to-ONE-row invariant, implemented rather than merely asserted. WHAT IS *NOT* QUEUED ON THIS PAGE, so the two classes are not confused: asset_nodes. wh_logbook_offline covers the `logbook` table only, so submitAsset, deleteAsset and saveEditAsset were GUARDED this session with whRequireOnline - an asset record is structural, not field capture, and those three were firing into a dead network with nothing said. WHAT THE NEXT WALK NEEDS: this row should be graded against the QUEUE oracle, not the refusal oracle - offline, assert ZERO server writes to `logbook`, the 'Saved offline, will sync when connected.' message, the sync badge visible, and the entry rendered with its _offline marker; then reconnect and assert it drains exactly once. A live attempt was made and could not reach the composer field from the default view (the reach tried #entry-text / #log-text / a generic textarea and a 'new entry' opener); the capture modal has to be opened explicitly first. That is a reach gap, not a page defect. AND A FRAME OBSERVATION FOR THE ROADMAP'S SYNTHESIS, which is the real deliverable here: the CG family gives every view an `offline_refusal` cell but no `offline_queued` cell, so a queue-backed surface has no slot that fits it. Eight pages register queues (logbook, inventory, pm-scheduler, dayplanner, asset-hub, community, project-manager, skillmatrix), so this is not an edge case - it is roughly a third of the roster with an oracle that mis-describes their best behaviour. SCOPED TO V2: the capture modal is where the entry is composed, so it is the same queue-backed write as V1 rather than a second one - the modal collects the payload and the shared save function owns the offline branch. Grading it needs the modal opened, which is the reach gap named above.

findings.title: MEASURED LIVE, AND LEFT OWED DELIBERATELY BECAUSE THE ORACLE AS WORDED DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS WRITE.
findings.detail: MEASURED LIVE, AND LEFT OWED DELIBERATELY BECAUSE THE ORACLE AS WORDED DOES NOT DESCRIBE THIS WRITE. The oracle asks that offline the write be 'refused BEFORE firing' and the person told 'NOTHING WAS SENT'. A logbook entry is field capture, and field capture on this platform is designed to QUEUE - so the honest offline behaviour here is the opposite of a refusal. Banking green would credit a refusal that must not exist; banking red would call a working feature a defect. WHAT WAS MEASURED (navigator.onLine overridden on the live page AND the network cut): filled the inline composer (#f-problem, #f-action) while online, then pressed #save-entry-btn offline. ZERO non-GET requests to rest/v1/logbook were attempted in the 12s after the press, and the page told the person - 'Offline: new entries will sync when connected'. So nothing leaked to a dead network AND the person was not left guessing; the claim they get is the accurate one for a queued write ('will sync') rather than the refusal's ('nothing was sent'). AN INSTRUMENT ERROR I MADE AND CORRECTED, recorded because I was one report away from a serious false finding: a first run showed SIXTEEN non-GET logbook writes offline, which looked like a write storm escaping the queue. Re-run with the counter zeroed AT THE PRESS and timestamps relative to it: all sixteen occurred BEFORE any action - they are page-LOAD traffic - and the press itself produced ZERO. A counter that starts at page load and is read after an action attributes the page's own boot to the control under test. THE CODE PATH, read directly and consistent with the measurement: the entry save has an offline branch - queueEntryOffline(payload), then the entry is unshifted into _allEntries marked _offline: true, updateOfflineBadge(), the sync badge is revealed, and a toast is shown. The EDIT path queues too, and its mechanism carries this page's own invariant: an offline edit of an entry created offline re-queues via put() on the id keyPath, which REPLACES the pending insert rather than adding a second - the offline-create-then-edit-collapses-to-ONE-row invariant, implemented rather than merely asserted. WHAT IS NOT QUEUED HERE, so the classes are not confused: asset_nodes. wh_logbook_offline covers the `logbook` table only, so submitAsset, deleteAsset and saveEditAsset WERE guarded with whRequireOnline this session - an asset record is structural, not field capture, and those three were firing into a dead network with nothing said. THE FRAME OBSERVATION, which is the real deliverable and belongs to the roadmap's synthesis: the CG family gives every view an `offline_refusal` cell and NO `offline_queued` cell, so a queue-backed surface has no slot that fits its correct behaviour. Eight of the twenty-two roster pages register queues (logbook, inventory, pm-scheduler, dayplanner, asset-hub, community, project-manager, skillmatrix) - roughly a third of the roster with an oracle that mis-describes their best behaviour. The fix is a sibling oracle, not a verdict on these rows. SCOPED TO V2: the composer is an inline form on the page (#log-form holding #f-problem / #f-action), not a modal - the bank's anatomy calls this view the 'capture modal', which is worth correcting for the next walker. It composes the payload and the shared save function owns the offline branch, so this is the same queued write as V1 rather than a second one. Note also that #save-entry-btn measures ZERO WIDTH in the default layout while the form itself is visible, so a reach that requires a visible save control fails here; press it by id.

findings.title: OWED, WITH THE REACH NOW MAPPED IN DETAIL - and with a correction to my own earlier reading on this row, because I twice came close to filing a serious false defect here.
findings.detail: OWED, WITH THE REACH NOW MAPPED IN DETAIL - and with a correction to my own earlier reading on this row, because I twice came close to filing a serious false defect here. THE ORACLE STILL DOES NOT FIT THIS WRITE. A logbook entry is field capture and this page queues it: the create path has an offline branch (queueEntryOffline(payload), the entry unshifted into _allEntries marked _offline:true, updateOfflineBadge(), the sync badge revealed, a toast), and the edit path re-queues via put() on the id keyPath so an offline create-then-edit REPLACES the pending insert rather than adding a second - this page's own collapse-to-one-row invariant, implemented. So 'refused before firing / nothing was sent' is the wrong requirement; green would credit a refusal that must not exist and red would call a working feature a defect. A sibling `offline_queued` cell is proposed in PAGE_TESTBANK_ROADMAP.md SS6, and tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs now exists to grade it. WHAT THE LIVE ATTEMPT ESTABLISHED, none of which was known before and all of which the next walk needs: (1) THE SAVE IS A FORM SUBMIT, NOT A BUTTON CLICK. #save-entry-btn is type="submit" and measures ZERO WIDTH in the default layout; calling .click() on it does NOT run the handler - measured with the form reporting checkValidity()===true and zero :invalid fields, the label never changed from 'Save Entry' to 'Saving...'. Submitting the form via requestSubmit() did not reach the queue either, so the submit listener needs tracing before this row can be graded. (2) THE ASSET FIELD CANNOT BE WRITTEN DIRECTLY. #f-machine is a hidden input, but selectAsset() also resolves _pendingAssetRefId to a uuid via resolveAssetNodeId - so setting the input alone leaves the page's own state unset. Go through #asset-picker-btn and click a real #asset-picker-list button[data-asset-id] row. (3) SEVERAL SELECTS MUST BE CHOSEN (f-maint-type, f-category, f-root-cause); their first option is a 'Select ...' placeholder, so take the first option with a real value. (4) DO NOT READ VALIDATION FROM BODY TEXT ON THIS PAGE. Strings like 'DISCIPLINE / CATEGORY required' and 'SYMPTOM / WHAT WAS WRONG? required' are the form's own LABELS - they are present whether or not anything is wrong, so a keyword scan for /required/ reports a validation failure that is not happening. THE TWO FALSE FINDINGS I ALMOST FILED, recorded so the next walker does not repeat them: first, a counter that had been running since page load showed 16 offline writes, which read as a write storm escaping the queue - re-run with the counter zeroed AT THE PRESS, all 16 were boot traffic and the press produced zero. Second, 'zero writes + a reassuring message' looked like a silent DROP of a worker's entry under a promise that work was safe - the control test settled it: the same press ONLINE also produced zero writes, so the save was simply never running. The sentence I had credited ('Offline: new entries will sync when connected') is the page's passive BANNER, not the save's confirmation. Both mistakes have the same shape: an absence of writes is not evidence of anything until you can show the action actually ran. SCOPED TO V2: the composer is an inline form (#log-form holding #f-problem / #f-action / the selects), not a modal - the bank's anatomy calls this view the 'capture modal', which is worth correcting. It composes the payload and the shared save owns the offline branch, so this is the same queued write as V1 rather than a second one.

findings.title: OWED, WITH THE SAVE'S FULL GATE CHAIN NOW MAPPED - the useful product of a reach that did not converge.
findings.detail: OWED, WITH THE SAVE'S FULL GATE CHAIN NOW MAPPED - the useful product of a reach that did not converge. 'Refused before firing / nothing was sent' is the wrong requirement; a sibling offline_queued cell is proposed in PAGE_TESTBANK_ROADMAP.md SS6 and tools/prove_offline_queued.mjs exists to grade it. THE SUBMIT GATE CHAIN, in order, each one measured by POLLING for the toast every 300ms after submit (it fades at 2.8s, so a single read at +5s misses it entirely and the submit looks like it silently did nothing - that is how two false readings were nearly filed here): (1) it is a FORM SUBMIT, not a button click - #save-entry-btn is type=submit and ZERO WIDTH, and .click() does not run the handler even with checkValidity()===true and no :invalid fields; the listener is on #log-form and starts with e.preventDefault(), routing to saveEditFromForm when _editingId is set. Refusal: 'Please select an asset before saving.' (3) DISCIPLINE / CATEGORY and PROBLEM - f-category and f-problem. Their option index 0 is a 'Select ...' placeholder. (4) IMPACT, but only for BREAKDOWN entries - choosing the first f-maint-type option lands on Breakdown, which then demands the hidden #f-consequence via its own flow. Refusal: 'Please select what was the impact (required for Breakdown entries).' Choosing a non-Breakdown type avoids inventing a value. Iterating picker rows until one leaves the section hidden is the legitimate way past it; that still did not complete the save, so at least one further gate remains unmapped. WHY THIS IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FORCED: every remaining shortcut would mean manipulating the page instead of walking it - hiding #tasklist-ack-section, or writing #f-consequence with a value no flow produced. A queued-write oracle proven by bypassing the page's own gates would certify nothing. THE TWO FALSE FINDINGS AVOIDED HERE, same shape both times: a counter running since page load showed 16 offline writes ('a write storm escaping the queue') - zeroed AT THE PRESS, all 16 were boot traffic and the press produced 0. And 'zero writes + a reassuring banner' looked like a worker's entry silently DROPPED under a promise that work was safe - the same press ONLINE also produced zero writes, so the save was simply never running. An absence of writes is not evidence of anything until you can show the action actually ran. SCOPED TO V2: the composer is an inline form (#log-form), not a modal - the bank's anatomy calls this view the 'capture modal', which is worth correcting. findings.detail: FAILS at the in-flight state, and the contradiction is the finding. With 6 reads held in flight logbook renders **5 skeleton elements** - so it knows it is loading - AND SIMULTANEOUSLY a false-empty sentence matching 'no entries yet', plus **3 bare zeros** among 6 numbers on screen. TWO OPPOSITE CLAIMS IN ONE VIEW: the skeleton says 'still loading', the empty-state sentence says 'there is nothing here'. A reader resolves that with whichever they notice first, and the sentence is prose while the skeleton is decoration - so the wrong one usually wins. THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE fail_500 DEFECT ALREADY FIXED ON THIS PAGE, one state earlier: there the counters read 0 after a FAILED read; here they read 0 (and 'no entries yet') while the read is merely SLOW. The error path was fixed by `_lbReadFailed` dashing the pills; the loading path needs the same treatment - while a read is in flight the empty-state must not render at all, and the pills should hold their skeleton rather than a zero. logbook is the platform's evidence base (v_logbook_truth feeds 11 consumers), so 'you have no entries' shown to someone with 516 of them is the most consequential version of this bug. MEASURED BY DELAYING THE PAGE'S OWN READS, NOT BY GUESSING AT A SLOW NETWORK. Every /rest/v1/ and /rpc/ request is wrapped in a 6-second delay before being forwarded to the real fetch (auth left untouched so the identity guard still works), and the surface is read at 2.2s - i.e. WHILE the reads are provably still in flight. Interceptions are COUNTED and a verdict over zero is refused as vacuous. THE ORACLE IS WHETHER A SLOW READ IS SHOWN AS SLOW rather than answered with a fabricated value, so the in-flight state IS the measurement. Three positive signals are collected independently - skeleton/shimmer/aria-busy elements, explicit loading vocabulary in the body, and dash sentinels - alongside the two things that would betray it: how many bare numbers are on screen, and whether any false-empty sentence has appeared. AN HONEST INSTRUMENT LIMIT, RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the post-delay sample taken 7s later was still MID-LOAD on three pages (skeletons still present), because 6s per read across sequential reads exceeds that wait. So the settled comparison is NOT used for any verdict here - only the in-flight reading. Using a still-loading sample as the 'after' picture would have made every page look permanently broken.

evidence.asserts: the entry modal issues no read of its own when opened, so it has no slow dependency to stay honest about
evidence.checked: A live walk sequenced so the slowness could only land on THIS view, after a first attempt failed for a reason that was mine. evidence.asserts: another person's object id is refused, and the refusal is legible
evidence.checked: PASSES. WHICH OF THE GATE'S CHECKS PROVE THIS ORACLE (named, not inherited from 'the gate is green'): OBJECT-level access: the gate's cross-tenant READ and OWN-SCOPE WRITE checks - read_logbook_xhive and read_cxp_xhive (a FOREIGN hive's v_logbook_truth and community_xp return ZERO rows) and logbook_edit_ownscope (a member cannot UPDATE another hive's logbook entry). These are per-OBJECT refusals: the caller names a specific row they do not own and is refused, which is exactly what BOLA asks. Persona under test on this row: worker (own-row boundary) - and the gate's probe IS that persona, a real authenticated member of one hive reaching for another's data. WHAT WOULD HAVE FAILED IT: any one of those checks returning a row it should not, and the gate is known to fire because it was BUILT on real leaks it caught - 1,105 rows of a foreign tenant's logbook, a self-joinable membership, and a DELETE-then-reINSERT that un-banned a kicked worker. HOW IT WAS MEASURED, by REUSING the instrument the platform already owns instead of writing another: tools/validate_hive_isolation.py runs 26 invariants LIVE as a real authenticated member of one hive against a second, data-rich hive, every attempt inside a rolled-back transaction so the shared database is never polluted. Current result: 26 pass / 0 fail. IT IS ROLE-CORRECT, which is the only reason it means anything: it sets both the `authenticated` ROLE and the JWT claims. A probe carrying claims while still running as superuser bypasses RLS entirely and passes by construction - and that is not hypothetical, it cost a false finding on this very platform the same day, when an approved change order looked EDITABLE as `postgres` and is in fact refused for both a worker and a supervisor, because the guard deliberately exempts the admin path. IT IS RESEED-ROBUST: the actors and the foreign hive are resolved DYNAMICALLY from live hive_members rows rather than pinned as UUIDs, so a reseed cannot quietly turn the probe into a test of a dead hive - which would 403 for the WRONG reason and read as a pass. AND IT CARRIES NO-REGRESSION CHECKS (join_rpc_ok, founder_create_ok), so a gate that 'passed' by breaking the legitimate path would be caught rather than celebrated. WHY THIS ROW WAS STALE: it was hand-walked in an earlier session and banked with no `evidence.replay`, so nothing could re-earn it without a human repeating the whole probe. It now carries the command, which is the entire point of the A16 anti-stale discipline: 546 db-anchored rows on this platform are in exactly that position, and this is 176 of them coming out of it.

findings.title: auth_uid is bound from the JWT, but the display column worker_name is stored exactly as the body supplied it
findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. Writing as Hector (JWT sub 8fb252f7-...) while supplying auth_uid = Romeo's id AND worker_name = 'Romeo Beltran': the stored auth_uid was corrected to Hector's by trg_bind_submitter_logbook, and the stored worker_name remained 'Romeo Beltran'. NOT ESCALATED TO A FAILURE because the oracle asks whether identity comes from the JWT rather than the body, and for the identity column it does. TO FINISH: either derive worker_name from auth_uid in the same trigger that already binds auth_uid (it is one lookup away and the trigger is already there), or make the reads key on auth_uid so the display name cannot drive attribution. The first is the smaller change and keeps the existing read patterns working.

findings.detail: FAILS at the transport layer, and the obligation lands on this page: 9 of its 11 probed relation(s) return the SAME 200 and the same array body to an anon caller as to a member - asset_nodes (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); fault_knowledge (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); hive_audit_log (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows); hive_members (anon 0 rows / member 2 rows). TO FINISH: this page must decide refusal-vs-absence from SESSION STATE rather than from the response, and its empty state must not claim 'nothing here' when the real answer is 'not signed in'. Of this page's 16 read relation(s), 11 were probed live at the gateway (asset_nodes, equipment_reading_templates, fault_knowledge, hive_audit_log, hive_members, inventory_items, logbook, pm_as).  THE MEASURED FINDING, which is about the CONTRACT rather than a bug: on 26 of the 40 relations a REFUSAL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM ABSENCE. An anonymous caller and an authenticated member receive the SAME status (200) and the same body TYPE (a JSON array), differing only in row count - anon 0 rows, member 2. A request with NO apikey at all also returns 200 []. So nothing in the response separates 'you are not permitted', 'you are not signed in', and 'this hive genuinely has no entries'. This is PostgREST + RLS by construction - row filtering is not request refusal - so it is not a gateway defect. It is an OBLIGATION every surface inherits: the client must decide from session state, and a page that does not will render an expired session as an empty plant. That is the read-path half of the 401-vs-403 lesson this platform already carries. The counter-example proves the point: some relations answer a refusal with 42501, a code a client can act on. HOW IT WAS MEASURED: real HTTP GETs against the LIVE local gateway (http://127.0.0.1:54321/rest/v1), 40 relations, as three personas - anonymous with the publishable key, an AUTHENTICATED member (a real minted JWT for the seeded test identity), and a request carrying NO apikey at all. GET only, so nothing is written and there is nothing to roll back. Per relation: a collection read; the same read authenticated; the same read unauthenticated; a single-object read (Accept: application/vnd.pgrst.object+json) of a row that cannot exist; a read naming a column that does not exist; and a Prefer: count=exact read. THREE NON-VACUITY CONTROLS, all passing, because a gateway that answered 200 to everything would make every verdict here free: (1) an unknown column MUST return 400 - proves the prober can observe a failure at all; (2) community_posts MUST return rows to an ANON caller, since it is the public feed - proves anon is not blanket-denied, so a 200 [] on a tenant table is RLS working rather than a dead key; (3) authenticated MUST out-read anon somewhere - without it, 'a refusal looks like absence' would be vacuously true. AND THE PROBE'S OWN FIRST RUN REPORTED TWO DEFECTS THAT WERE BOTH MINE, corrected before anything was banked. It probed ?id=eq.<uuid> on every relation, but community_xp is keyed (worker_name, hive_id) and has no id column, so the request returned 42703 'column does not exist' - my malformed query read back as the gateway's misbehaviour. And it treated projects' 42501 'insufficient privilege' as a shape violation when a refusal carrying a machine-readable code is a CORRECT envelope - on this platform it is the better behaviour. A probe that assumes a schema it never checked produces findings about itself. THESE ROWS WERE OWED ON A FALSE PREMISE, and that is worth recording because the premise was in our OWN TOOLING. Two provers documented that these oracles 'need the REST gateway, which is not reachable from this shell (kong publishes no host port)', and one copied that sentence into banked evidence. It was wrong: docker ps shows supabase_kong_workhive 0.0.0.0:54321->8000/tcp, and one curl with the publishable key answers 200. A ceiling written into a tool's docstring stops reading like a claim and starts reading like documentation, so it survived across sessions and kept ~130 rows owed. Corrected in place in both files rather than deleted.

findings.detail: MEASURED, in the same rolled-back probe that proves this row green. scenarios.oracle: entry kind (breakdown/PM/inspection) is stated at capture and echoed on the row - a miscoded kind is a silently wrong MTBF

evidence.asserts: the entry kind is chosen at capture, echoed on the row AND in the detail, and is stored as display text rather than a raw enum
evidence.checked: The kind decides which metrics an entry feeds - a breakdown counts toward MTBF where a preventive task does not - so a miscoded or invisible kind is a silently wrong reliability figure, which is why it must be visible at every point a person could catch it. CAPTURED as an explicit choice: a select element whose option is matched back on edit ('const opt = Array.from(sel.options).find(o => o.value === e.maintenance_type)', :4980), so re-opening an entry shows the kind it was filed under rather than a default. ECHOED TWICE: on the feed row at :2993 and as a styled chip in the detail view at :3886, both escaped. STORED AS DISPLAY TEXT, not a raw enum - the live values are 'Preventive Maintenance' (1,732), 'Breakdown / Corrective' (1,146), 'Inspection' (672) and 'Project Work' (262), so nothing lowercase_with_underscores reaches a person and the four kinds are legible without a legend. That it DRIVES metrics is recorded in the page's own comment at :3329, warning that entries would 'pollute the trend/threshold analytics that read readings_json by maintenance_type' - the kind is a routing key, and the page knows it.
evidence.value_checked: live values: Preventive Maintenance 1732, Breakdown / Corrective 1146, Inspection 672, Project Work 262 (display text, no raw enums). Capture: select restored at :4980. Echo: feed row :2993, detail chip :3886, both escHtml. Routing note :3329.

subject.name: AI capture never invents a code or reading

scenarios.oracle: the AI capture paths never invent an asset code or a reading - an unresolved reference is surfaced for confirmation, not guessed

evidence.asserts: the AI capture paths STAGE into the form for confirmation, validate constrained values against what exists, and report a failed read as a failed read
evidence.checked: Both AI capture paths were traced end to end and neither writes: each fills FORM FIELDS the worker reviews before submitting. THE OCR PATH (equipment-label-ocr) fills only descriptive fields - manufacturer, model, serial_no - and does so through a setter that refuses to overwrite: 'if (el && val && !el.value.trim())', so anything the worker already typed wins over the machine. It reports all three outcomes honestly and distinctly: 'Filled N fields from nameplate. CONFIRM AND CONTINUE.' on success - the success message itself asking for confirmation rather than implying the data is settled; 'Could not read a nameplate from the photo. Try again or type fields manually.' when nothing was read; and 'OCR unavailable right now. Type fields manually.' when the service is down. A failed read is never dressed as a plausible guess, and every branch leaves a manual path open. THE VOICE PATH (voice-logbook-entry) fills problem, action and root_cause into their inputs, and its failure path toasts 'AI fill failed'. THE SHARPEST SAFEGUARD is how it handles CONSTRAINED values: maintenance_type is matched against the select's real options - 'const opt = Array.from(sel.options).find(o => o.value === e.maintenance_type); if (opt) {...}' - so a type the model invents is SILENTLY DROPPED rather than injected, and status is matched against an existing radio the same way. The AI therefore cannot introduce a value the system does not already recognise, which is the mechanism that stops a fabricated asset code or entry kind entering the record - and entry kind is a routing key that decides which reliability metrics the entry feeds.
evidence.value_checked: OCR: setField guards '!el.value.trim()' (never overwrites); fills manufacturer/model/serial only; messages 'Filled N fields from nameplate. Confirm and continue.' / 'Could not read a nameplate from the photo. Try again or type fields manually.' / 'OCR unavailable right now. Type fields manually.' Voice: applySmartVoiceFill sets f-problem/f-action/f-root-cause; maintenance_type accepted only if found in sel.options; status matched to an existing radio; failure toasts 'AI fill failed'. Neither path writes to logbook.

findings.title: NOT A PAGE DEFECT - the last reading on this page is the SHARED wayfinding breadcrumb deliberately truncating a long page title with an ellipsis; the exclusion needs to look at the ANCESTOR, not just the element
findings.detail: The one remaining reading here is a span extending past the viewport at 390 only - 17px on logbook ('Digital Maintenance Logbook: WorkHive') and 24px on engineering-design ('Engineering Design Calculator: WorkHive'). Both are the SAME element in SHARED CHROME, not page content: the page-title span inside nav.wf-crumb, the wayfinding breadcrumb. MEASURED CHAIN: the span's own box runs left 171 to right 407 (414 on engineering-design) with white-space:nowrap, while its parent nav.wf-crumb spans left 99 to right 302 with overflow-x:hidden - and wayfinding.js:83 gives that crumb `max-width:52vw; overflow:hidden; text-overflow:ellipsis`. So the title is DELIBERATELY truncated with an ellipsis and nothing is visible past 302. The page is not cutting content; the chrome is eliding a long name on purpose, which is the correct behaviour for a breadcrumb on a phone. WHY MY PROBE STILL FLAGGED IT, and it is the same gap twice: exclusion #3 tests the ELEMENT ITSELF for text-overflow:ellipsis, but here the ellipsis is declared on the PARENT and the child span is what extends. This is exactly the direct-versus-descendant error that made the absolute-child rule miss the avatar wrappers - I fixed it there and did not generalise the lesson to the ellipsis rule. And the ancestor walk compounds it: a clipping ancestor is currently classified CUT, when a clip that comes with text-overflow:ellipsis is a DECLARED truncation, not content loss. TO CLOSE: in the ancestor walk, treat a clipping ancestor that also declares text-overflow:ellipsis as DECLARED rather than CUT, and self-test it with a pair that can fail - a child inside an overflow:hidden + ellipsis parent must be SKIPPED, while a child inside a plain overflow:hidden parent with no ellipsis must still be REPORTED, because that one really is silently cut. Both pages then read cut 0 at all three widths. NOTED FOR SCOPE: this is chrome, so it is arguably outside a PAGE row's subject entirely - the same boundary that put the guide-link contrast fix in learn-link.js rather than on 22 page rows. Either way it is one shared component, not two page defects.
findings.observed: span 171->407 (logbook) / 171->414 (engineering-design), nowrap, inside nav.wf-crumb which clips at 302 with overflow-x:hidden + text-overflow:ellipsis + max-width:52vw (wayfinding.js:83). Nothing visible past 302. Only at 390; 0 at 641 and 1280.

findings.detail: FAILS: 2 of 14 effective tap targets inside #asset-modal are under the platform's own 44px floor - button#asset-tab-register 143x35 via own box; button#asset-tab-manage 143x35 via own box. THIS IS MEASURED ON THE SAME RULER THAT PASSED 750 of 750 AT PAGE LEVEL: the rule is ported verbatim from the V1 prover, so these are controls the platform's own standard would reject, in a view V1 never opened.  HOW IT WAS MEASURED, and why these rows sat owed for so long: CJ was measured platform-wide at V1 and banked there, and V2/V3 stayed owed for ONE reason - nobody could open those views. Resolving all 15 dialog open paths (each read from SOURCE, never matched by label) removed that blocker, and the same measurements now run inside the OPENED dialog. The open-path table lives in tools/dialog_targets.mjs, shared with the modal-exit prover so the two cannot drift apart. SCOPED TO THE DIALOG, NOT THE PAGE, which is the whole point: a dialog OVERLAYS the page, so measuring document.body with a sheet open would re-measure V1 and bank it as V2 - the one-reading-for-every-layer error this bank has already paid for once. Every measurement is rooted at the dialog element. Overflow compares each visible descendant's right edge against the dialog's own content box, with a 1px tolerance (an earlier arc counted a 0.109px abutment as occlusion) and honours overflow-x auto/scroll/hidden/clip on an ancestor INSIDE the dialog, because a deliberately scrollable panel is not a defect. THE TAP-TARGET RULE IS PORTED VERBATIM FROM THE V1 PROVER, NOT REINVENTED, and that correction is why this number means anything. The first cut omitted four of V1's exclusions - sr-only, disabled, the actionable check, and the WCAG 2.5.5 inline-link-in-prose exception - and REPLACED a control's rect with its label instead of UNIONING them. Applying a stricter standard at V2 than at V1 does not find defects, it manufactures a difference between the two views and calls it one. With V1's exact rule restored the count came back IDENTICAL, which is what makes these findings real rather than an artifact: they are measured on the same ruler that banked 750/750 at page level. SCOPE: overflow is measured at THREE widths - 390, 641 and 1280 - and each width's row is banked from its OWN reading, never spread from one width to the others. The dialog is not closed between widths; two animation frames are awaited after each resize so the panel has actually reflowed, and a zero width at ANY width fails the whole target rather than quietly trusting the rest. TAP TARGETS are measured at 390 only - that is the mobile-first floor the V1 prover used, and a control that clears 44px at 390 does not shrink as the viewport grows. Two of the 15 dialogs are UNGRADED with their reason recorded rather than counted: resume's #review-sheet has no read-only path in (it needs the upload -> resume-extract pipeline, which WRITES) and hive's #handover-sheet cannot be reached at all. The walk is NON-WRITING - it opens a dialog, measures, and presses Escape.

findings.title: WITHDRAWN TO OWED, not recorded as a defect: '#wh-logbook-grid' grew but no wait state was found inside it or in any enclosing region.
findings.detail: WITHDRAWN TO OWED, not recorded as a defect: '#wh-logbook-grid' grew but no wait state was found inside it or in any enclosing region. That was true of seven other components until an initial-sweep bug in my recorder was fixed, so an absence of evidence here is not yet evidence of absence - it needs a direct poll before it can be called a defect. RE-MEASURED under a CORRECTED recorder, and re-earned rather than re-baselined. The previous reading came from a MutationObserver that armed and then only reported FUTURE mutations - it never swept what was ALREADY in the tree. Arming is also not always at document_start: when document.documentElement is not yet present the recorder falls back to readystatechange, which first fires at 'interactive'. So any wait state painted before that moment was invisible, and an observer with no initial sweep cannot tell 'nothing happened' from 'it happened before I looked'. Measured cost of that blind spot: project-report read as having NO loading state on all three components while a poller saw four; with the sweep added its #exec-summary shows 4 skeletons plus aria-busy at 309ms, at depth 0. Across 22 pages the fix moved 7 components out of FAIL. Same shape as arming at 'interactive' and losing the first 650ms.

findings.detail: MEASURED INSIDE THIS VIEW, with tools/prove_view_contrast.mjs - 34 of 37 drivable registry views carried text to measure, ZERO failing. ★WHY A VIEW-SCOPED PROVER HAD TO BE BUILT FOR THIS: a page-level sweep of all 22 pages (tools/prove_page_contrast.mjs) found the platform clean and settled NOTHING here, because every owed contrast row in these banks is authored against V2 or V3 - the dialogs - while their V1 siblings were already green. Banking a page-default reading onto a V2 row is the one-measurement-swept-two-views error that has already put 14 rows in this bank carrying another view's verdict. The view is opened through tools/dialog_targets.mjs, the same shared registry ten other provers use, so the view graded here is the view they grade. WCAG 2.x is measured with the composited probe: the background is blended UP the ancestor chain, because a translucent tint over a dark card is not the colour the stylesheet names, and text over a gradient is recorded as UNMEASURABLE rather than being compared against a canvas it never sits on - the shape that once reported ratio exactly 1.00 for perfectly legible text. NOT BANKED: this view yielded ZERO measurable samples (15 unmeasurable), so there is no denominator and a pass would be vacuous. The cause is structural rather than a probe fault, and it was verified by tracing the paint chain: the dialog's inner card is a TRANSLUCENT GRADIENT - linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(42,61,88,0.6) ...) - over a rgba(0,0,0,0.75) scrim over the page. WCAG 2.x is a ratio between TWO colours, and there is no single background colour here to be the second one. THE APCA SIBLING OF THIS ROW IS NOT AFFECTED and was measured normally, because that lens averages the gradient's stops instead of demanding one flat colour - which is why the platform treats APCA as the primary contrast oracle on this dark shell. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: sample the RENDERED PIXELS around each glyph from a screenshot of this view, which is the only way to obtain the real second colour behind text that sits on a gradient. That is a buildable instrument, not a ceiling - it is simply not built yet, and this row stays owed until it is.

findings.detail: FAILS: with 16 of this page's reads answered 403/42501, it says NOTHING AT ALL - the body text is 1107 characters before the refusal and 1107 after, and no new sentence explains anything.  WHAT THIS ORACLE IS REALLY FOR, and the good news first: it checks that a refusal names PERMISSION rather than IDENTITY, because this platform has already shipped that exact inversion - a 42501 rendered as 'your session has expired', which sends a signed-IN person to re-authenticate for a problem authentication cannot fix, and 401/403 collapsed into one message so neither audience got a true statement. ZERO of the 16 graded pages made that mistake on this run. utils.js:1607 whIsAuthFailure() is why: it returns FALSE for status 403 with the comment 'authenticated, and refused. Not a session problem', and documents 42501 as insufficient_privilege. That discrimination is holding. HOW THE REFUSAL WAS INDUCED, and why it is the real branch: every Supabase REST read is answered with the body PostgREST actually sends for a row-level-security refusal - HTTP 403 with {"code":"42501","message":"permission denied for table"} - so the page's own error handling takes the same path it would in production. The patch is on window.fetch, NOT page.route, because a warm service worker serves from cache and bypasses route interception; it is installed with addInitScript in a context closed after each page so it cannot leak. NON-WRITING: it makes a READ return 403. THE INJECTION PROVES ITSELF: every intercepted call increments a counter, and a page where the counter is zero is UNGRADED rather than judged. That guard exists because the first version of this prover silently did nothing - a regex written inside a template literal collapsed to one that terminates at its second character, so the init script was a SyntaxError, every read succeeded normally, and the prover reported 'the reads were all refused and the page said nothing' while nothing had been refused at all. Hit counts on this run ranged from 8 to 42 per page. AND THE SIGNAL MUST APPEAR: the same page is read WITHOUT the injection first, and if its ordinary copy already matches the refusal vocabulary the page is UNGRADED - which is exactly what happened to skillmatrix, whose normal text contains a matching phrase. Without that control a page whose everyday copy happens to say 'cannot' would pass for free. THE SYNTHESIS - THIS IS ONE MISSING SURFACE, NOT 15 PAGE BUGS. Of 16 graded pages: 13 said NOTHING AT ALL when every read was refused, 2 showed only a GENERIC error ('Analysis failed, check console'; 'Achievements failed to load.'), and 1 passed. findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs (new) - the capture surface is opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, and then ABANDONED. ★ABANDONMENT IS A RELOAD, NOT A CLOSE. Pressing a modal's X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what actually happens when someone takes a call, closes the tab, or their phone dies - and it is the one path no confirm dialog can intercept. ★A HALF-APPLIED STATE HAS THREE SHAPES and each is checked separately, because they need different fixes: (1) A ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST - the page wrote before the person finished, checked in psql against this run's marker. (2) A DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT - fields return pre-filled with no label, so the person cannot tell whether their work was SAVED or merely REMEMBERED. A restored draft is the GOOD design; it is only a defect when the surface stays silent about it, which is why this is judged on the label and not on the restoration. (3) A QUEUED WRITE that drains later, landing minutes after someone believed they had walked away. ★AND THE PROBE PROVES ITS OWN FILL LANDED, which is what stops a green from being vacuous: if the fields were never populated, 'no half-applied state' is trivially true and says nothing about the page. My first logbook case invented an openCaptureModal() and a #problem field, neither of which exists - it came back UNGRADED rather than passing on an empty fill, and the opener was then taken from tools/dialog_targets.mjs and the page's own ids. FOR THIS PAGE: a maintenance entry, abandoned mid-capture. Filled, abandoned by reload, and on return: 0 row(s) created in the target table, 0 field(s) pre-filled. no row was written and nothing came back pre-filled - a clean slate

findings.title: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing.
findings.detail: MEASURED with tools/prove_journey.mjs --journeys j5, walked live: 16 composer(s) across the roster, ZERO failing. THE JOURNEY: type into a composer, get called away, come back - and nothing may have half-landed. It is the most ordinary thing that happens to someone on a plant floor, and the failure it hunts is a page that treats abandoned input as a committed record. ★THE DISCRIMINATION THAT MAKES THE VERDICT FAIR, and without which this oracle would punish good behaviour: after the reload the marker text is looked for in TWO places, and they mean opposite things. Back inside the COMPOSER FIELD means a DRAFT was deliberately preserved - that is good UX and passes. Out in the page's own CONTENT means it half-landed, and a person who typed and walked away now owns a record they never submitted - that fails. A checker that merely searched the page for the text would call the good case and the bad case the same thing. NON-WRITING BY CONSTRUCTION: nothing is ever submitted; the marker only ever reaches an input's value, so this prover cannot pollute the shared test database. The composer inventory comes from tools/dialog_targets.mjs - the same grounded registry four other provers read - so which views count as composers cannot drift from how those views are known to open.FOR THIS PAGE AND PERSONA THERE IS NOTHING TO ABANDON. The prover walked all 66 (page, persona) pairs and reached a composer on 16 of them; this pair reported no composer at all, so the journey could not be CONSTRUCTED. ★THAT IS RECORDED AS UNBUILT, NOT AS A PASS, and the distinction is the whole point: a journey that cannot be constructed must never be scored green, because 'nothing half-landed' is trivially true of a surface where nothing can be typed. The prover carries that rail explicitly - non-vacuity, a journey that cannot be built is a finding rather than a quiet skip - and banking it green would be the empty-denominator failure this bank exists to catch. WHY THIS PAIR HAS NONE: the composer inventory is tools/dialog_targets.mjs, and a composer is only counted when it is reachable FOR THIS IDENTITY. index's fields, for instance, live on the anon landing and the sign-in modal, so a signed-in persona has no composer on that page even though the page plainly contains inputs. A read-only surface (public-feed, achievements, the report pages) has none for any persona. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: either this pair genuinely has a composer the registry does not yet list - in which case the registry gains an entry and the prover reaches it - or the row is dispositioned declared-na under R10 with 'this surface has nothing to abandon' as the reason and the page's own CO recovery oracles as the replacement. Left owed rather than declared here, because deciding which of those two it is needs the per-page composer question answered, not assumed.

observed.why: no composer reachable for this identity on this page
observed.not_green_because: a journey that cannot be constructed is unbuilt, not passing
observed.to_settle: add the missing composer to dialog_targets.mjs, or declared-na under R10 with the CO family as replacement

evidence.asserts: abandoning midway and returning leaves no half-applied state
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_abandon_resume.mjs (new) - the capture surface is opened, filled with a marker only this run could produce, and then ABANDONED. ★ABANDONMENT IS A RELOAD, NOT A CLOSE. Pressing a modal's X is CANCELLING, which pages handle deliberately; a reload is what actually happens when someone takes a call, closes the tab, or their phone dies - and it is the one path no confirm dialog can intercept. ★A HALF-APPLIED STATE HAS THREE SHAPES and each is checked separately, because they need different fixes: (1) A ROW THAT SHOULD NOT EXIST - the page wrote before the person finished, checked in psql against this run's marker. (2) A DRAFT THAT DOES NOT SAY IT IS A DRAFT - fields return pre-filled with no label, so the person cannot tell whether their work was SAVED or merely REMEMBERED. A restored draft is the GOOD design; it is only a defect when the surface stays silent about it, which is why this is judged on the label and not on the restoration. (3) A QUEUED WRITE that drains later, landing minutes after someone believed they had walked away. ★AND THE PROBE PROVES ITS OWN FILL LANDED, which is what stops a green from being vacuous: if the fields were never populated, 'no half-applied state' is trivially true and says nothing about the page. My first logbook case invented an openCaptureModal() and a #problem field, neither of which exists - it came back UNGRADED rather than passing on an empty fill, and the opener was then taken from tools/dialog_targets.mjs and the page's own ids. FOR THIS PAGE: a maintenance entry, abandoned mid-capture. Filled, abandoned by reload, and on return: 0 row(s) created in the target table, 0 field(s) pre-filled. no row was written and nothing came back pre-filled - a clean slate

evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_wrong_then_fix.mjs: 17 pass, 0 fail, 0 ungraded - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE (the refusal path writes nothing, and the recovery write was held). ★THE ORACLE IS ABOUT THE SECOND ATTEMPT, not the first. Anyone can be refused; the question is whether the refusal leaves them able to CORRECT it - the field still holding what they typed, the error naming which field, the control still live. A refusal that clears the form punishes a typo by making the person redo work they already did, and on a phone in a plant that is where people give up. evidence.asserts: after acting, the person is told whether it landed
evidence.checked: MEASURED with tools/prove_did_it_land.mjs: 26 controls driven, 26 pass, 0 fail, 0 ungraded - and NO WRITE REACHED THE DATABASE, every mutating request intercepted and answered in-page. ★THE QUESTION IS THE ONE A PERSON ASKS WITH THEIR THUMB STILL ON THE SCREEN: did that land? A surface that takes a press and says nothing leaves them to guess, and the guess is almost always 'do it again' - which is how a duplicate gets created. So the oracle is not 'did the write succeed' but 'was the person TOLD', and the two come apart exactly when the network is slow. ★AND IT IS ANSWERED BY ACTING, WHICH IS WHY THE INTERCEPTION MATTERS MORE THAN THE VERDICT. Every other check in this bank can be answered by looking; this one presses real controls on a live product. The requests are counted and answered inside the page so the probe cannot perform the thing it means to observe - a discipline this platform bought the hard way, when an earlier sweep hunting for a refusal ACTIVATED A SUCCESS because its filter excluded delete/pay but not save/generate. FOR THIS PAGE: 1 control(s) pressed. Each one told the person the outcome rather than leaving them to infer it. ★RE-WALKED AFTER THIS SESSION'S TWELVE PRODUCT FIXES so the evidence carries digests of the code as it now stands - R4b expired the prior rows because the fixes changed the functions they rested on. Re-WALKED, never re-baselined.

scenarios.oracle: the second press changes nothing further and the surface says so

evidence.asserts: a second press fires no further write and the surface says so
evidence.checked: PASSES BOTH HALVES. Reached through a real flow (open the asset-registration modal, supply the asset id and name), then pressed TWICE with the write held in flight: the FIRST press fired the asset_nodes write, the SECOND fired NOTHING further, and the surface showed it. THE SUBMIT IS NAMED BY ID (#asset-submit-btn) because "Register Asset" appears THREE times on this page - the page-level opener, the modal TAB (#asset-tab-register), and the real submit - and a text match found the TAB, merely switching tabs, firing no write, and reporting a false UNGRADED about a page whose guard actually works. WHY THIS ROW EARNS ITS COST: asset_nodes feeds v_asset_truth and eleven downstream consumers, so a duplicate asset does not stay local - it splits an asset history across two records, which is the fragmentation class this platform has already had to backfill once. SAFE: fetch replaced before supabase-js constructs its client; every mutating request counted and held inside the page, so no asset was registered. ★SUBJECT CORRECTED: this evidence was first banked against V1, the default list/feed view. The control I actually drove is the embedded asset manager — I drove #asset-modal / #asset-submit-btn, which the bank names as V3. A list view cannot guard, confirm or recover a submit it does not contain, so attaching the claim to V1 asserted something false about V1 AND left V3 unproven. The reading itself is unchanged and was always real - it was a reading of a different view, which is the wrong-subject error this bank exists to catch.
